title: Sable and the Contact
premise: Oscar Whitlock, a disgraced intelligence analyst living under a polished false identity in a coastal town, spots an anomaly no one else can see: Flight 447's records vanish mid-flight while the plane is still airborne. As she digs, she realizes the erasure is tied to a passenger list she once compiled—and that her own fabricated past is unraveling alongside it. Hunted by the agency that burned her and the contractor who wants the list buried, Oscar must decide whether to trade her most dangerous secret—the true identity of a mole she protected years ago—for a seat on a dawn extraction flight out of the country. In the end, she gives up the secret to save an innocent witness, misses the flight by minutes, and discovers that belonging means staying to face what she erased rather than escaping it.
about_author: Sable Thornbury is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent a decade writing briefings she now freely admits were fiction of a different kind. She lives near a small airport, where she watches departures and takes notes.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Oscar Whitlock's POV. We meet her in her rented cottage: three identities deep, go-bag packed, routine rehearsed. A quiet morning ritual establishes her paranoia and competence. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness—she has made invisibility an art and calls it safety.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the marina café she idly checks a flight tracker out of habit and watches Flight 447's record evaporate while the aircraft is still transmitting altitude data. She assumes a glitch, then confirms it across three databases. Beat: the thrill of pattern recognition waking something dormant in her.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Remembers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with a brief interlude from local fisherman Dev Anand, her only friend. Dev notices her distraction; she deflects with practiced charm. She pulls her old access credentials from a cached drive. Beat: guilt—using old skills feels like relapse.

chapters.title: The Passenger List
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Reconstructing fragments, she identifies nine names aboard 447, including one she recognizes: Elena Marsh, a translator whose disappearance Oscar helped bury five years ago. Beat: dread hardening into resolve—this isn't coincidence; it's cleanup.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, Three Exits
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Oscar's POV. How she was bounced: scapegoated for a leaked assessment, then quietly cut from two contractors. Introduces Marcus Hale, the handler who burned her. Beat: bitterness curdling into understanding that her exile was engineered.

chapters.title: A Man Who Orders Decaf
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A watcher appears in town—a man too neat, asking questions at the café. She runs counter-surveillance on instinct and loses him, but knows he'll be back. Beat: fear sharpening into focus; the game has found her.

chapters.title: Elena's Voice
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She finds a voicemail Elena left before boarding, referencing 'the Whitlock file.' Someone aboard knew Oscar's real history. Beat: vertigo—her lie and the vanished flight are entangled.

chapters.title: Hale Calls
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Oscar and Marcus Hale. Hale offers reinstatement in exchange for whatever she's found; she lies smoothly, but he names her cottage street. Beat: the sick recognition that invisibility was always permission he granted.

chapters.title: Dev Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. He confronts Oscar gently about the strangers in town and the bruises on her knuckles from a parking-lot scuffle. She gives him a half-truth. Beat: warmth and its cost—belonging requires honesty she can't afford.

chapters.title: The Mole I Kept
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, flashback. The secret worth killing for: years ago she identified a mole inside a partner service and sat on the name to protect someone she loved. That name connects directly to Flight 447's passenger list. Beat: shame surfacing after long burial.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She calculates odds, maps the extraction flight leaving at dawn from a private strip two hours north, and weighs trading the mole's name for a seat. The watcher nearly catches her retrieving a dead-drop. Beat: cold pragmatism cracking under exhaustion.

chapters.title: Elena Isn't Dead
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following the voicemail trail, she finds Elena alive in a safehouse clinic, memory fragmented from an 'accident.' Elena holds the corroborating evidence Oscar needs—but doesn't remember Oscar betrayed her silence. Beat: hope tangled with terror of being recognized.

chapters.title: What You Did to Me
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Fragments return; Elena remembers Oscar's face from the debrief room and confronts her. Oscar confesses the betrayal partially. Beat: raw confrontation—memory as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: Contractors at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Hale's team raids the harbor looking for her; Dev covers her escape without knowing why, getting detained. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallizes—innocent people pay for her secrets.

chapters.title: The Interrogation of Dev Anand
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Held in a rented office, Dev refuses to give Oscar up, insisting she's just a neighbor who fixes his nets' accounts. His stubborn decency shames the interrogator. Beat: belonging demonstrated, not claimed.

chapters.title: Terms at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Captured briefly by Hale, she negotiates: the mole's name for Elena's freedom and a seat on the dawn flight. Hale agrees too easily. Beat: suspicion beneath relief—she knows how deals like this end.

chapters.title: The Name in the Envelope
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Alone with the envelope containing the mole's name, she drafts two versions—one true, one poisoned. Flashbacks to the person she protected. Beat: the weight of truth as a thing you can hold and hand over.

chapters.title: Dawn Strip
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the airfield, she sees Elena loaded onto the same flight as leverage, not rescue. Hale demands the envelope. Oscar hands over the poisoned version and stalls as sirens rise. Beat: adrenaline and clarity—she chooses the witness over the exit.

chapters.title: Flight Leaves Without Her
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The extraction lifts off at dawn with Hale aboard; Oscar stays behind with Elena as federal investigators—tipped by Dev's interrogator's conscience—swarm the strip. Beat: loss and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In a windowless room, she gives the true name, the full account, and her own crimes, choosing truth over the polished lie for the first time. Beat: catharsis through confession; memory reclaimed instead of managed.

chapters.title: The Harbor in Winter
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Months later, Oscar—under a plea deal and her own name at last—returns to the cottage. Dev doesn't ask questions; he hands her a net to mend. Beat: quiet belonging earned honestly.

chapters.title: Sable and the Contact
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, epilogue. A letter arrives from Elena, memory still patchy but forgiveness offered conditionally: come visit, tell me everything again. Oscar packs a bag—not a go-bag, just luggage—and books a flight that exists in every database. Beat: resolution—visibility chosen, memory shared, belonging begun.
